title: Partner approval gap review and snippet kit
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a focused preflight for partner marketplace submissions that frequently stall during legal/technical review. It pairs a compact acceptance-gap checklist with ready-to-use tile and feature-copy variants teams can drop into partner portals. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth during vendor review windows and accelerate first-publication from weeks to days.

Audience:
- GTM product and partner managers preparing listings
- Solutions engineers who validate technical gates
- Legal/compliance reviewers looking for required artifacts

How to use this kit:
1) Run the Acceptance Gap Checklist with the partner. Mark any failures as an action item with an owner and target date.
2) For any missing deliverables, use the Copy Snippets section to draft the listing tile and short description immediately.
3) Attach required artifacts (screenshots, SSO test user, SAML metadata, KMS encryption note) to the submission folder and link them in the partner ticket.

Compact Acceptance Gap Checklist (fast pass items, yes/no):
- Business/Commercial
  - SKU mapped and approved by pricing (yes/no)
  - Trial entitlement or free-tier configured (yes/no)
  - Billing account sample payloads attached (yes/no)
- Security & Compliance
  - Data residency statement present (yes/no)
  - KMS/HSM integration plan or consumer-managed-key option documented (yes/no)
  - SOC/ISO attestation or third-party audit summary present (yes/no)
  - Vulnerability/incident contact info included (yes/no)
- Identity & Access
  - SSO flow documented (SAML/OIDC) and test account available (yes/no)
  - Least-privilege role diagram or table attached (yes/no)
- Technical & Operations
  - API endpoint contract and example requests provided (yes/no)
  - Metrics/telemetry contract (events + formats) supplied (yes/no)
  - SLA/uptime target defined for marketplace offering (yes/no)
  - Support/oncall contact and escalation matrix attached (yes/no)
- Product UX/Assets
  - 2–3 tile imagery variants uploaded (PNG, 1200x627) (yes/no)
  - Short tile copy (20–40 chars) drafted (yes/no)
  - Long description (300–900 chars) drafted and tech-reviewed (yes/no)
  - Demo or trial provisioning flow documented (yes/no)

Common blocking patterns we see (notes for reviewers):
- Missing a clear billing SKU or ambiguous trial entitlements (causes legal to pause).
- No SSO test account or expired metadata — stalls SSO certification.
- Generic claims ("enterprise-grade") without specific attestations or performance numbers.
- Tile copy that repeats platform brand language rather than partner value (marketplace reviewers ask for customer-facing clarity).

Copy Snippets: quick variants to copy/paste into marketplace forms. Keep characters tight for titles and flexible for long descriptions. Edit bracketed fields before use.

Short title (20–30 chars) — variants:
- Fast LLM inference for apps
- Predictable LLM serving, managed
- Low-latency model inference (private)

Short subtitle (40–80 chars) — variants:
- Dedicated inference pools with SLA and telemetry
- Serve open models at scale with autoscaling and cache
- Private VPC deployments, KMS-ready, enterprise SLAs

Long description (300–450 chars) — draft: 
Redwood Inference delivers predictable, production-grade LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship features faster with model-aware routing, automatic KV/prefix caching, and per-route telemetry. Choose dedicated capacity for predictable throughput or private VPC for regulated workloads; integrate with your SSO and KMS to meet enterprise controls.

Feature bullets (short list, 3–6 bullets):
- Multi-mode serving: hosted API, reserved capacity, private VPC
- Cost controls: batching, quantization recommendations, and cache hints
- Observability: token-level cost, latency traces, rollout history
- Reliability: automated fallbacks and canary rollouts

Suggested call-to-action variants:
- Start a free trial — provision a sandbox in minutes
- Request a private demo and SLA options
- Try a pre-provisioned dedicated pool (contact sales)

Required assets checklist (upload before submission):
- Tile image (1200x627) + 1 alternative crop
- 800x600 screenshot showing console or flow
- Demo provisioning runbook (PDF) or video link
- SAML metadata file or OIDC client details + test credentials
- Billing SKU and example billing payload (JSON)
- Data residency + encryption short statement (one page)
- Support & escalation contacts (ODR format)

Low-effort mitigations for common gaps (what PMs can do immediately):
- If no SSO test account: create a temporary test tenant and include explicit rotation expiry date for reviewers.
- If no KMS plan: add a consumer-managed key toggle and a one-paragraph encryption note describing at-rest encryption and key control.
- For billing SKU confusion: attach a simple mapping table of product features to SKU codes and entitlement names.

Stakeholders and suggested owners:
- Listing copy + imagery: GTM product manager (owner)
- Technical acceptance + SSO/KMS tests: solutions engineer
- Legal/compliance docs: partner legal reviewer
- Final submission and follow-up: partner manager or channel ops

Timeline template (example for 10-day push):
- Day 0: kickoff + acceptance gap run (owner assigned)
- Day 1–2: partner supplies missing artifacts and test accounts
- Day 3: copy and imagery finalized, draft listing created
- Day 4: SSO/KMS and billing validation by SE
- Day 5: legal checks and final edits
- Day 6–9: internal QA and marketplace scheduler window
- Day 10: publish or schedule publish

Open questions / unresolved items
- Which sandbox tenant should we use for cross-partner SSO test accounts (consolidate in a shared spreadsheet)?
- Do we require a minimum performance metric for "dedicated" SKU (tokens/sec baseline)? Proposal: set a soft baseline and publish it as guidance.

Next steps (for the immediate sprint):
- Assign owners for any gap items from the last three partner runs (Marco Ruiz)
- Create a shared SSO test-tenant spreadsheet and circulate to solutions-eng (Samir)
- Push finalized short-copy variants to the asset repo and tag for marketplace (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets/pull/78)

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers to include in the ticket body
- Link to listing draft + asset folder
- Attach SAML metadata or OIDC client info + creds
- Confirm SKU mapping and billing payload example
- Include support contact and target SLA
- Point legal to data residency page and a one-paragraph encryption note

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Consider a tiny script to validate image dimensions and presence of alt text before submission (engineering ask).
- Add a marketplace-specific copy style guide snippet in next iteration (voice, do/don't).
- Track time-to-publish metric for each partner and target median <= 7 days.
